name: Skild S1
summary: S1 is Skild's foundation model built explicitly as an in-context learner. A single video demonstration — seen or unseen during training, short or long — is supplied at inference and the model performs the task without any weight update. Skild reports unseen ten-minute tasks executed from one human video at 66% success against a 9% baseline. It is the deployment vehicle for Skild Brain, the company's omni-bodied policy intended to run across robot morphologies rather than one embodiment, and it follows a year in which Skild raised a $1.4B Series C and acquired Zebra's robotics arm to put the model into warehouses.
innovation: In-context task specification from human video, removing both fine-tuning and on-robot teleoperation from the loop of teaching a new task.
Ten-minute horizons from a single demonstration, where prior one-shot work operated on single skills.
matters: If a new task costs one video instead of a data collection campaign, the economics of deploying robots change more than any accuracy gain would.
limits: Company blog only, with headline numbers and no paper, task list or independent evaluation.
Announcement date is reported inconsistently across sources (18 vs 25 August 2026); the 66%-vs-9% comparison baseline is unspecified.
lineage: Latent-action pretraining from human video, recast as inference-time in-context conditioning.
